notes.title: Beach Relaxation VR Development Suspended
notes.content:
I've received a number of queries regarding this project lately, so I thought it best to clear the air and bring everyone up to date on things (Better late than never!).

When I set out on this project, I was hoping to get it finished in a year's worth of spare time. It would be a simple single-player island simulator where you could destress by just watching the water, painting, building sand castles, or resting in a hammock. Much of the work would be optimizing for performance so even computers that weren't built yesterday could handle it alright...or so I thought.

When I gave a copy of what I had done so far to a few testers, the unanimous verdict was that it was unusable on the Vive headset. As the simulation was built in Unreal Engine 4, I found that so hard to believe that I purchased one for myself to see it first hand. And it was terrible. It was more like watching a slideshow than a simulation; and a number of objects were in the wrong place, rendering incorrectly and even turned around by ninety degrees! On top of that, I tried submitting the app through the official Oculus validator only to return failure with issues that I could not reproduce on my home computer.

The two events led me to believe this would not be done in a year, that there were nuances to VR development I never expected to contend with, and that this was not as casual an undertaking as I expected. I'm no stranger to spending years on passion projects, but in this case I made the decision to turn my attention back to other projects that interested me more.


[h2]Is this the end?[/h2]

I wouldn't go as far as saying that. The current passion project I'm working on, an online sports brawler, won't be done before late 2025. Maybe after that project enters maintenance mode I may come back to this. Or maybe I will find someone to help me reboot this project in Unreal Engine 5, which has many improvements over the previous engine. I really did enjoy watching the trailer and actually painting on the VR canvas in the simulation, after all.

notes.title: Seeking Testers For Beach Relaxation VR!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=JYMWcZX-qBo;full][/previewyoutube]

Beach Relaxation VR is an escape to your own private island in virtual reality where you can relax, paint and build sandcastles from the comfort of home.

Listen to the soothing waves from your beach chair as you watch the seagulls play near the water. Lie in a hammock as the palm trees wave in the gentle ocean breeze. Paint a beautiful sunset on a canvas that you can take anywhere with you. Build a sand castle, or even your own little sand house on the beach that will never be ruined by an oncoming wave. Gaze at the moon and the stars from a hidden tropical enclave.

In exchange for a few hours of your valuable time, you will receive a [b]FREE[/b] beta key to immerse yourself in the experience for as long as you like. If your feedback is detailed and helpful, you may also receive a key for the full version after it's released!

To apply for your [b]FREE[/b] beta key, all you have to do is [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf36v3zVtugLAhYRCxxHCUOYRKA-9gU0imjwJjVPhsUiWizzQ/viewform]go to the beta key giveaway portal and submit your e-mail address[/url]. You should receive your beta key within 24 hours.

After that, post your feedback and bug reports on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1483230/discussions/]Beach Relaxation VR Discussions Board[/url].

So what are you waiting for? Join the Beach Relaxation VR beta and send us your feedback today!

[b]Hurry, keys are limited and we may quickly run out![/b]
